t: This is the Lewisham Arthouse, which began as a Carnegie library building. It now serves a different purpose, but the shape of a public library is still there. It was designed by Sir Alfred Brumwell Thomas, an English architect who trained at the Westminster School of Art. He became an exponent of Baroque Revival architecture, a style that was popular for public buildings in the early years of the twentieth century. Look for that confident, ornamented civic character in the design.
